guitar.guitaristsText: Steve Hackett / Mike Rutherford / Daryl Stuermer
guitar.evidence: Steve Hackett (early era) was known for Gibson Les Pauls; Mike Rutherford and touring guitarist Daryl Stuermer covered guitar in the Phil Collins era. No single guitar is iconic for the band's commercial 80s hits listed here.

tone.target: tight funky clean-crunch with quacky mids
tone.profile: tight funky clean-crunch with quacky mids
tone.summary: A clean signal chain using light compression, a Boost for punch, followed by the US Deluxe amp model, paired with a US 2x12 cab to achieve a bright, funky, quacky sound.

rig.name: Genesis - I Can't Dance - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain tight rhythm definition.
Add percussive attack and sustain for funky rhythm chanks.
Provide a subtle edge-of-breakup and increase the perceived punch.
Optional subtle grit for added character without heavy fuzz.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is generally too aggressive; it's kept off but available for slight breakup if needed.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the clean Fender/JC style amp for bright, quacky tones.
Provide a bright and focused cabinet sound suitable for funk rhythms.
Enhance the quacky mids and tighten the low end.
Add a small amount of natural room ambience without sounding lush or wide.
blocks.gap: The 'Room' module is used sparingly to meet the requirement for an ambience effect while keeping it dry and controlled.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR for better realism and tonal depth while maintaining the bright funk character.

proposals.reason: Improve cabinet realism for a more authentic clean tone.
